 ← Back to Match Centre Hull v Ipswich 
 Hull vs Ipswich confirmed line-ups see Gary O’Neil retain the side that drew with Nottingham Forest , with Emersonn leading the attack and Saša Lukić missing out as he continues his recovery from injury.
 Jaden Philogene and Abdul Fatawu both start for the visitors, while Jack Clarke, Daizen Maeda and Zian Flemming are among the substitutes. Nobel Mendy is back in Hull’s starting XI.
 Advertisement 
 Kick-off is at 3pm GMT on Saturday 31 October at the MKM Stadium. Our  Hull vs Ipswich viewing guide  explains the broadcast and highlights details.
 Ipswich confirmed line-up: O’Neil keeps faith with Forest XI
 Ipswich’s official team announcement  confirms O’Neil has made no changes following the 1–1 draw with Forest.

 Christian Walton starts in goal, with captain Dara O’Shea joined in defence by Abdoul Ouattara, Issa Diop and Leif Davis.
 Advertisement 
 Florentino Luís partners Exequiel Palacios in midfield. Julio Enciso, Fatawu and Philogene support Emersonn, with Clarke again available from the bench.
 Ipswich XI:  Walton; Ouattara, Diop, O’Shea (c), Davis; Florentino, Palacios; Fatawu, Enciso, Philogene; Emersonn.
 Substitutes:  Scherpen, Furlong, Greaves, Matusiwa, Núñez, Clarke, Maeda, Akpom, Flemming.
 Hull confirmed line-up: Mendy starts
 Mendy’s inclusion settles one of Hull’s selection questions from the build-up. Our  earlier Hull vs Ipswich injury update reported that the defender had returned to contention following a groin problem.
 The teams published in  the Guardian’s matchday coverage  also confirm starts for Lewie Coyle and Oli McBurnie. Lucas Herrington is among the substitutes.  live 
 Advertisement 
 Hull XI:  Tzolakis, Coyle, Ajayi, Egan, Mendy, Iroegbunam, Belloumi, Giles, Slater, McBurnie, Stroud.
 Substitutes:  Phillips, Morita, Gelhardt, McNair, Norton-Cuffy, Herrington, Crooks, Mouzakitis, Cho.
 Why is Saša Lukić missing?
 Ipswich say Lukić remains absent while recovering from injury. His omission means Florentino and Palacios continue together in midfield, with Azor Matusiwa and Marcelino Núñez among O’Neil’s alternatives.
 The confirmed selection follows uncertainty over whether Lukić would be ready for the trip. He is not included in the starting XI or the nine-player bench.
